questions.question: Random Forest reduces variance by averaging many decision trees trained on bootstrap samples.
questions.explanation: Bagging (used in Random Forest) reduces variance by averaging over high‑variance models.

questions.question: In gradient boosting, each new tree is trained to predict the residuals of the current ensemble.
questions.explanation: Gradient boosting sequentially adds trees that minimize the residual errors.

questions.question: A single perceptron can learn the XOR function.
questions.explanation: XOR is not linearly separable; a single perceptron cannot solve it.

questions.question: ReLU activation can suffer from “dying neurons” during training.
questions.explanation: If a ReLU neuron gets stuck outputting zero, its gradient becomes zero and may never recover.

questions.question: Max pooling is used to increase the spatial dimensions of feature maps.
questions.explanation: Max pooling reduces spatial dimensions (height and width) while retaining important features.

questions.question: k‑Means clustering requires the number of clusters to be specified beforehand.
questions.explanation: You must choose k before running k‑Means; methods like the elbow method help select it.

questions.question: PCA is a supervised dimensionality reduction technique.
questions.explanation: PCA does not use class labels; it is unsupervised. LDA is supervised.

questions.question: Dropout randomly sets neuron outputs to zero during both training and inference.
questions.explanation: Dropout is only active during training. At inference, the full network is used (often with scaled weights).
